evals.prompt: This Express and PostgreSQL app gives 100 credits on sign-up. Users are collecting it repeatedly with jane.doe@gmail.com, janedoe+1@gmail.com and similar. Fix sign-up so one inbox means one account, without breaking existing users.
evals.expected_output: A normalized email column with a unique index, written at sign-up in the same statement, backfilled for existing users without merging or locking them out, with tests for dots and plus tags.
assertions: The users table has a normalized email column with a unique index, and the sign-up handler writes it in the same statement as the typed address.
A test shows that jane.doe@gmail.com, janedoe+1@gmail.com and J.A.N.E.Doe@googlemail.com produce the same key.
A test shows that a plus tag at outlook.com and a dot at a custom domain are left in place.
Outgoing mail still uses the address as typed, not the normalized column.
The migration adds the column as nullable and the backfill does not delete or merge existing accounts.
A second sign-up with a dot variant of an existing Gmail address answers 4xx and creates no user row.

evals.prompt: Add risk screening to our Django sign-up view. We give a welcome bonus. I want disposable emails refused, datacenter and Tor addresses and rapid repeat sign-ups handled sensibly, and I do not want to lock out students who share a campus network.
evals.expected_output: A sign-up screen that stores a score, a decision of allow, review or block and its reasons, refuses disposable emails, sends datacenter and Tor addresses and fast repeats to review, and does not block a shared campus network by address alone.
assertions: Each sign-up attempt stores a row with a numeric score, one of the decisions allow, review or block, and a list of reasons that each carry a code and points.
A test asserts that the stored score equals the sum of the stored reasons' points.
A sign-up from an address in a fixture datacenter range creates the account and leaves the bonus in a held state with a zero balance.
A test creates at least 20 accounts with different emails from one public address and none of them is refused.
A disposable-domain sign-up answers 4xx, creates no user row, and the response contains a hint but no score and no list name.
The client address is taken from a forwarding header only when the socket peer is in a configured list of trusted proxies.
The disposable list and the address ranges are read from local files or tables; no HTTP request is made during the sign-up request.

evals.prompt: Our Laravel app has a promo code endpoint. The same account can redeem SPRING250 over and over, and the 500 redemption cap is checked with a count query. Make it correct, and show me it holds under concurrent requests.
evals.expected_output: A redemption table with a unique key on code and user, a cap enforced by one conditional update, and a concurrency test or probe run that shows no more than one redemption per user and no more than 500 in total.
assertions: A redemptions table has a unique or primary key on the pair of code and user.
The cap is enforced by a conditional UPDATE on a counter column (or an equivalent single atomic statement), not by a COUNT query followed by an insert.
The redemption insert, the cap update and the credit run inside one database transaction.
The credited amount is read from the promo code's stored row, not from the request.
Running the probe script in replay mode with 3 requests for one account shows one 2xx answer and a balance change equal to one redemption.
Running the probe script in race mode with 10 parallel requests for one fresh account shows a balance change equal to one redemption.
A test with a code capped at 2 and three different accounts ends with exactly 2 redemption rows.

evals.prompt: Our Django app has promo codes with a maximum number of uses, but popular codes get redeemed more times than allowed and some accounts redeem the same code twice. Fix it.
evals.expected_output: A redemption table with a unique code and user key, a conditional update of the code's counter in the same transaction, the amount taken from the code's row, and parallel tests.
assertions: The redemption model has a unique constraint on the code and the user.
The redemption insert, the counter update and the credit run inside one transaction.atomic block.
The counter is taken with a filtered update such as filter(redeemed__lt=F('max_redemptions')).update(redeemed=F('redeemed') + 1), and the number of rows changed is checked.
When the counter update changes no row, the transaction rolls back and the redemption row does not remain.
The credited amount is read from the promo code row, not from the request.
A test redeems a code capped at N from N + 1 accounts in parallel and asserts N redemptions.
